task: PM1 - per-page orphan_start_frac telemetry + arpipe orderqc
headline_result: 84 of 194 documents have at least one page with orphan_start_frac > 0.03 while the document-level score remains <= 0.03.

implementation.metric_source: verify.order_quality() internals, refactored (not reimplemented) into shared helpers _reconstruct_paragraphs_tagged and _score_paragraphs, reused by both order_quality() (document level, unchanged output) and order_quality_by_page() (new, page level)
implementation.page_attribution_rule: a reconstructed paragraph is attributed to the physical page containing its first non-whitespace source line; page tags are threaded through paragraph reconstruction itself, never recovered from offsets in the joined text
implementation.page_array_schema: qc.orphan_start_frac_pages: list[float|None], length == document total physical page count (profile.n_pages), index i corresponds to 1-based physical page i+1; null = not measured (outside MD&A span, or fewer than 2 reconstructed paragraphs attributed to that page); 0.0 = measured, no orphan starts observed
implementation.full_width_block_rule: textlayer.page_has_full_width_block(pdf_path, page_no): reuses the existing COLUMN_FULLWIDTH_FRAC=0.60 threshold and _blocks() geometry _column_cut already uses internally to decide a block masks the gutter; returns None when the page has no extractable block geometry (e.g. a scanned page, or the annual_report.pdf copy is unavailable)
implementation.diagnostic_threshold: verify.PAGE_ORPHAN_DIAGNOSTIC_THRESHOLD = 0.03, a fixed constant independent of (though numerically equal to, today) verify.ORPHAN_START_FRAC_MAX; never recalibrated, never read by grade()/build_reasons()

interpretation.aggregate_hiding: The document-level orphan_start_frac hides a page-level spike (a page strictly over the 0.03 diagnostic threshold while the document average reads <= 0.03) in 84 of 194 documents (43.3%) - more than four in ten documents that would look clean on the document-level metric alone actually contain at least one page whose reading order is as bad as, or worse than, documents already flagged low/order_scrambled.
interpretation.concentration: Bad pages are not spread evenly: 135 of 194 documents (69.6%) have at least one bad page, but those 135 documents produce 706 bad pages between them (median ~5 bad pages per affected document), and the page-score distribution is heavily right-skewed (median page score across all 2728 measured pages is 0.0; even P75 is only 0.0312, just above the diagnostic threshold, while P95 reaches 0.125 and the single worst page scores 0.6471) - most measured pages are clean, and the badness concentrated in a a minority of pages within a majority of documents.
interpretation.full_width_block_cooccurrence: Of the 706 bad pages, 429 (60.8%) carry a block wider than 60% of the page text band (the known _column_cut full-width-masking mechanism) and 199 (28.2%) do not; the remaining 78 (11.0%) could not be measured (no extractable block geometry, typically a scanned/OCR page). A full-width block co-occurs with a bad page more often than not, but nearly three in ten bad pages show no such block - co-occurrence is not proof of causality, and no causal claim is made here.

caveats: A concurrent, unrelated Claude Code session was observed actively modifying files in this same repository (segment.py, triage.py, new test files) during this work. Both the baseline and after-PM1 extraction runs were verified via sha256 checkpointing to have used byte-identical segment.py/triage.py/patterns.py/config.py/ocr.py/store.py/models.py throughout each run (workers import these once at process start; no live-reload risk). Any content difference between the two runs could therefore only come from the PM1 diff itself, and the regression check found none.

The full pytest suite carries one pre-existing failure (tests/test_pipeline.py::test_p33_is_given_below_not_pointer) in segment.py logic never touched by PM1; it fails identically with PM1 code present or reverted.
